source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
One Sterling campus publishes 114 MW of IT capacity, 7.1 percent of Virginia's disclosed data center load, while most of the state's 330 mapped facilities disclose nothing.

Disclosure is the exception in Virginia, not the rule. Of 330 mapped data center facilities, only 25 publish a megawatt figure, and those 25 total 1,603 MW. Ashburn AS01's 114 MW ranks third among them. That ranking describes what has been disclosed, not necessarily what has been built.

For AI, published IT capacity is the closest available proxy for compute. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 114 MW implies roughly 2,850 racks. That arithmetic belongs to the reader, not the operator. The facility does not publish its workload mix or tenant configuration, so whether those racks hold training clusters or something else is unknown.

The record also stops short on power. LEED certification addresses efficiency, not where the electricity comes from or how it reaches the site. The grid connection point, whether supply comes from existing utility service or new generation, and whether the full 114 MW is allocated or available are all unpublished. Without them, this campus's role in Virginia's power constraint cannot be assessed.
